subject: Follow-up: BAA scoping, SOC2 artifacts, and hosting recommendation for Aurelia Health POC
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@aureliahealth.com>, procurement@aureliahealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + immediate asks for hosting / audit scope

Hi Alex / Aurelia procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — appreciate the clarity on the POC goals. Quick recap and a few items we need to scope hosting and compliance precisely: 

- Business requirements we captured: ingestion of EHR-derived events (small PHI payloads), realtime inference for care triage, SLA target ~150ms p50 for small requests, steady-state ~30 qps with 120 qps bursts.
- Compliance asks you mentioned: BAA required for any PHI, SOC2 Type II attestation for vendor onboarding, and a pre-procurement audit window for evidence.
- Hosting preference you signaled: prefer Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, but willing to evaluate Private VPC if contract/legal requires on-prem or customer-managed network.

What we need from your side to finalize recommendation and pricing:
1) Confirm whether the PHI flows will include patient identifiers (yes/no) and whether storage of PHI is required beyond transient processing.
2) Expected steady-state qps and daily token volume (our rough number above helps; a spreadsheet is fine).
3) Target go-live date for the POC and any audit windows (e.g., internal security review date).

I've attached a short audit checklist to show the SOC2/BAA artifacts we typically provide. Karthik (cc) will scope the infra recommendation once we get the items above; Monica (I’ll loop in on procurement next) will coordinate contract/BAA steps.

Next steps: can you reply with the three items above? If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up with our security lead tomorrow.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- audit_checklist_v1.pdf (pdf, 48KB)
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@aureliahealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + immediate asks for hosting / audit scope

Thanks, Mina — great demo. Quick answers below: 

1) PHI scope: yes, payloads will include patient identifiers for matching (MRN, name) and short clinical notes. We do NOT plan to store long-term PHI in the vendor platform beyond 7 days for the POC (we will confirm retention during procurement).
2) Load: steady-state ~25-35 qps, expect 100k tokens/day with bursts up to 120 qps during some batch windows.
3) Timeline: target POC kickoff in early June; procurement/security review scheduled for the week of June 7 (internal).

Hosting preference: we prefer Dedicated capacity to start (predictable latency and cost), but legal asked us to include Private VPC as an option if BAA negotiations require stronger networking guarantees. Please confirm whether Dedicated + BAA is a supported combination and what encryption/key management options we have.

I've attached our internal hosting requirements spreadsheet for reference.

Alex Mercer
Head of Product Engineering
Aurelia Health

Mina / Monica / Alex —

Thanks for the details, Alex — helpful. My recommendation for the POC: start on Dedicated capacity with BAA in place. Rationale: the POC needs predictable latency and throughput (your qps and burst profile match our Dedicated pools), and Dedicated allows us to provide encryption-at-rest with customer-key options and shorter lead time than a Private VPC build. Private VPC is viable if legal insists on customer-managed networking or on-prem routing, but it will add ~1-2 weeks for architecture and cost signoff.

SOC2 / audit artifacts we can provide quickly (I can assemble these in ~72 business hours):
- SOC2 Type II attestation (redacted) or recent synopsis
- Control matrix mapping relevant controls to our runtime (CC6, CC7 equivalents)
- Network architecture diagram showing isolation for Dedicated pools
- Key management overview (KMS + HSM options) and encryption-at-rest policy
- Sample audit log extracts and retention policy
- Incident response plan excerpt and contact list
- Data retention/ERASURE workflow description for PHI (transient processing flow)

Private VPC feasibility and cost: estimate 7-10 business days to produce a customer-specific runbook and a pricing sheet; this includes network topology, peering/vpn requirements, and an uplift for operational runbook and SLAs. If you need a preliminary cost ballpark faster we can provide a delta estimate in 48 hours.

Next suggested steps:
1) Alex: confirm retention window for POC (you mentioned 7 days) in writing so we can include it in the BAA draft.
2) Monica: I’ll hand over the artifact bundle once I assemble it; please confirm any legal contact/DocuSign routing for BAA.
3) Mina: after Alex confirms retention, we send a single reply with recommended hosting, artifact ETA, and a DocuSign BAA starter link.

Attaching the SOC2 artifact checklist we will use.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
